name: Diffuse Lighting Models
text:
# Diffuse Lighting Models
## Overview
Diffuse lighting models calculate surface illumination by simulating light scattering, providing the primary visual cue for surface orientation and shape in ray-marched and rasterized rendering [G]. This family distinguishes itself from sibling methods like [Distance Color Blending](791-distance-color-blending.md) and [Specular and Reflective Shading](14299-specular-and-reflective-shading.md) by focusing exclusively on non-specular reflectance, often serving as the base layer for more complex shading [G].

## Shared principles
All methods in this family operate on a surface point $\mathbf{p}$ and its associated geometric data, primarily the surface normal $\mathbf{n}$, as detailed in [Lighting and Shading Models](2055-lighting-and-shading-models.md) [G].

## Subtopics

### [Phong Shading with SDF Normals](1977-phong-shading-with-sdf-normals.md)
Applies the [Phong reflection model](#22228-phong-reflection-model.md) to [SDF](#1466-signed-distance-fields-sdf.md) surfaces, distinguishing itself from [Lambertian Lighting in SDF](2023-lambertian-lighting-in-sdf.md) by including specular highlights and from [Blinn-Phong Shading in Volume Rendering](2809-blinn-phong-shading-in-volume-rendering.md) by using the exact reflected light vector rather than the half-vector approximation. Choose it when a shinier appearance with precise [specular reflections](#5690-specular-reflection.md) is required.

### [Lambertian Lighting in SDF](2023-lambertian-lighting-in-sdf.md)
Calculates pure diffuse illumination by [clamping](#11530-clamping.md) the dot product of the normal and light direction to zero, focusing solely on the diffuse component unlike [Phong Shading with SDF Normals](1977-phong-shading-with-sdf-normals.md) or [Blinn-Phong Shading in Volume Rendering](2809-blinn-phong-shading-in-volume-rendering.md) which include specular highlights. Choose it for physically plausible, matte shading that reveals surface [curvature](#11695-curvature.md).

### [Blinn-Phong Shading in Volume Rendering](2809-blinn-phong-shading-in-volume-rendering.md)
Applies the Blinn-Phong model to volume data, using the half-vector approximation for specular highlights which is computationally cheaper than calculating the reflection vector, and differs from [Lambertian Lighting in SDF](2023-lambertian-lighting-in-sdf.md) by including specular and ambient components. Choose it for efficient glossy surface simulation in volume rendering.

### [Gouraud Shading](4645-gouraud-shading.md)
Computes lighting colors at mesh vertices and linearly interpolates them across facets, solving the faceted appearance of polygonal approximations by creating continuous [color gradients](#16944-fire-color-and-opacity-curves.md), unlike Phong shading which interpolates normals. Choose it for performance-critical rasterized rendering of curved surfaces.

#### Flat Shading

### definition
- [S1, unofficial] A shading model assuming uniform lighting where light surrounds an object equally in all directions.

### code
- [S1, unofficial] glShadeModel(GL_FLAT)

### pitfall
- [S1, unofficial] Flat shading diminishes the three dimensionality of the scene.

## Background
The concept of flat shading was formalized in early graphics APIs like OpenGL, which provided `glShadeModel(GL_FLAT)` to specify uniform lighting across primitives [S1, unofficial]. [Gouraud shading](#4645-gouraud-shading.md), also known as smooth shading, was introduced to provide subtle color changes across surfaces by interpolating vertex colors, assuming light comes from a particular direction [S1, unofficial]. These models are foundational in visualizing data, such as in Fire Dynamics Simulation tools like Smokeview [S1, unofficial].

## Sources
[S1] Smokeview (Version 6) A Tool for Visualizing Fire Dynamics Simulation Data Volume II : Technical Reference Guide, https://doi.org/10.6028/nist.sp.1017-2, fetched 2026-10-26 (unofficial)
